newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee sees 18-year low in jobless rate.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee sees 18-year low in jobless rate.

text.p: Tennessee's unemployment rate dropped to 4.4 perccent in August, its lowest rate since the state began keeping seasonally adjusted figures in 1978, state officials said Friday.
That was down from 4.9 percent in July and 5.4 percent a year ago.
The improvement was partly due to a decline in the workforce, which shrank by 10,700 in August to 120,800, state labor officials said. At the same time, the number of jobs increased by 2.5 percent.
Eighty of the state's 95 counties reported lower jobless rates in August than in July and 14 had higher unemployment rates. One county, Shelby, was unchanged at 4.1 percent.
Williamson County had the state's lowest unemployment rate for August, 2 percent, while Lewis County had the highest, 15.5 percent.
